content.title: About
content.content: Biscuit is a light, airy cake made from eggs, sugar, flour, and a small amount of fat. It has a soft, slightly sweet texture and is often used as a base for cakes, desserts, and layered sweets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Biscuit originated in Europe in the 19th century as a variant of light, leavening‑free cake.
Traditional biscuit is prepared using the “foam” method, where eggs and sugar are beaten into a thick mousse before gently folding in flour.
Biscuit is frequently used in confectionery to create “sponges” – thin layers that can be stacked and shaped into complex structures.
In some countries the biscuit is called a “soft cake” because of its tender crumb.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Classic biscuit contains minimal butter, making it less calorie‑dense than many other cookies.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Biscuit provides a quick source of energy thanks to its simple carbohydrate content.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The porous structure aids digestion, making biscuit suitable for people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Biscuit is usually made from wheat flour, so it may trigger reactions in individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sugar in biscuit can raise blood glucose levels, so people with diabetes should limit consumption.

items.title: Short shelf life
items.content: Because of its high porosity, biscuit quickly loses moisture and can become dry; store it in an airtight container.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Biscuit can be enjoyed on its own, soaked in syrups, used as a cake base, sliced and served with fruit, berries, cream, or ice cream. It is also commonly layered in desserts such as parfaits.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store biscuit in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage keep it in the refrigerator, or freeze it if you need to preserve freshness and prevent drying out.
